```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
devtools::load_all("llrem", quiet = TRUE)
load("study3_results.RData")

ACTIVE_PROVIDERS <- c("bedrock_claude", "bedrock_llama")
provider_names   <- c(bedrock_claude = "Bedrock/Claude",
                      bedrock_llama  = "Bedrock/Llama")

conditions <- list(
  list(id = "predict_obs", label = "Predict (obs. history)"),
  list(id = "random_obs",  label = "Random roleplay (obs. history)"),
  list(id = "sender_obs",  label = "Sender roleplay (obs. history)")
)
condition_ids    <- vapply(conditions, `[[`, character(1L), "id")
condition_labels <- vapply(conditions, `[[`, character(1L), "label")

split_key <- function(key) {
  pkey <- ACTIVE_PROVIDERS[startsWith(key, paste0(ACTIVE_PROVIDERS, "_"))]
  list(pname = provider_names[[pkey]],
       cid   = substring(key, nchar(pkey) + 2L))
}

provider_palette <- c(
  "Empirical"      = "#2166AC",
  "Bedrock/Claude" = "#1B7837",
  "Bedrock/Llama"  = "#762A83"
)

rem_formula <- Surv(time = time1, event = occurred) ~
  Imitation + Repetition + RecInitiation + Recencylog + IOviolation + NTriadic +
  strata(time2)

stat_terms <- c("Imitation", "Repetition", "RecInitiation",
                "Recencylog", "IOviolation", "NTriadic")
term_order <- rev(stat_terms)

all_nodes    <- sort(unique(c(edgelist$sender, edgelist$receiver)))
base_riskset <- llrem:::get_base_riskset(NULL, all_nodes)
```

## Overview

This report summarises the results of Study 3, which compares event sequences
generated by two LLM providers (Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 and Meta Llama 3.1
70B, both accessed via AWS Bedrock) against the empirical Militarized Interstate
Dispute (MID) conflict sequence. Each provider was run under three query
conditions, producing 1,000-event sequences. Results are evaluated in two ways:
(1) Cox proportional hazards REM coefficients and (2) sufficient statistic means.

**Empirical baseline:** `r nrow(edgelist)` events, `r length(all_nodes)` actors.

---

## Empirical REM Coefficients

```{r emp-coefs}
ec <- round(coef(rem_empirical), 3)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Term = names(ec), Coefficient = as.numeric(ec)),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Empirical REM coefficients (Cox proportional hazards, MID dataset)"
)
```

The signs reflect established findings in conflict research: states repeat prior
targets (**Repetition** > 0), reciprocate recent initiations (**RecInitiation**
> 0), target salient recent adversaries (**Recencylog** < 0, decay),
avoid IO-norm violations (**IOviolation** < 0), and — crucially — *avoid*
attacking the enemies of their adversaries (**NTriadic** < 0).

---

## 1. REM Coefficient Comparison

```{r coef-plot, fig.height=5.5}
extract_coefs <- function(model, source, condition) {
  s <- summary(model)$coefficients
  data.frame(
    term      = rownames(s),
    coef      = s[, "coef"],
    lower95   = s[, "coef"] - 1.96 * s[, "se(coef)"],
    upper95   = s[, "coef"] + 1.96 * s[, "se(coef)"],
    source    = source,
    condition = condition,
    row.names = NULL,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

emp_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(condition_labels, \(cl)
  extract_coefs(rem_empirical, "Empirical", cl)))

llm_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(results), function(key) {
  if (is.null(results[[key]])) return(NULL)
  p    <- split_key(key)
  clbl <- condition_labels[match(p$cid, condition_ids)]
  extract_coefs(results[[key]]$rem, p$pname, clbl)
}))

coef_df <- rbind(emp_rows, llm_rows)
coef_df$term      <- factor(coef_df$term,      levels = term_order)
coef_df$condition <- factor(coef_df$condition, levels = condition_labels)
coef_df$source    <- factor(coef_df$source,
                             levels = c("Empirical", "Bedrock/Claude", "Bedrock/Llama"))

plot_xlim <- local({
  v <- c(coef_df$coef, coef_df$lower95, coef_df$upper95)
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  q <- quantile(abs(v), 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)
  c(-q, q) * 1.05
})

ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = coef, y = term, colour = source,
                    xmin = lower95, xmax = upper95)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_linerange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(position   = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = provider_palette) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = plot_xlim) +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Coefficient (log hazard ratio)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 9),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines"))
```

```{r coef-table}
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(results), function(key) {
  p  <- split_key(key)
  cf <- round(coef(results[[key]]$rem), 3)
  data.frame(Provider  = p$pname,
             Condition = condition_labels[match(p$cid, condition_ids)],
             as.data.frame(t(cf)),
             check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
emp_row <- data.frame(Provider = "Empirical", Condition = "—",
                      as.data.frame(t(round(coef(rem_empirical), 3))),
                      check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(rbind(emp_row, tab), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "REM coefficients by provider and condition")
```

## 2. Sufficient Statistic Comparison

REM coefficients can be unstable when a sequence is short or when one covariate
has near-perfect separation. The sufficient statistic means — the average value
of each covariate across realized events — are a more direct and numerically
stable measure of whether the LLM sequence shares the structural properties of
the empirical one. Dashed lines show empirical values; points show LLM
condition means.

```{r suffstat-plot, fig.height=5}
emp_sm <- compute_seq_stat_means(edgelist, rem_formula, base_riskset)[stat_terms]

llm_sm <- lapply(names(results), function(key) {
  tryCatch({
    s <- compute_seq_stat_means(results[[key]]$sequence, rem_formula, base_riskset)
    s[stat_terms]
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
})
names(llm_sm) <- names(results)
llm_sm <- Filter(Negate(is.null), llm_sm)

stat_df <- do.call(rbind, c(
  list(data.frame(term = names(emp_sm), mean_val = as.numeric(emp_sm),
                  source = "Empirical", condition = "Empirical",
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)),
  lapply(names(llm_sm), function(key) {
    p <- split_key(key)
    data.frame(term     = names(llm_sm[[key]]),
               mean_val = as.numeric(llm_sm[[key]]),
               source   = p$pname,
               condition = condition_labels[match(p$cid, condition_ids)],
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
))

stat_df$term      <- factor(stat_df$term,      levels = term_order)
stat_df$condition <- factor(stat_df$condition, levels = condition_labels)
stat_df$source    <- factor(stat_df$source,
                             levels = c("Empirical", "Bedrock/Claude", "Bedrock/Llama"))

emp_s <- stat_df[stat_df$source == "Empirical", ]
llm_s <- stat_df[stat_df$source != "Empirical", ]

ggplot(llm_s, aes(x = mean_val, y = term, colour = source)) +
  geom_vline(data    = emp_s,
             mapping = aes(xintercept = mean_val),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = provider_palette[levels(llm_s$source)]
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Mean covariate value across realized events", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text      = element_text(size = 9),
        panel.spacing   = unit(0.8, "lines"))
```

```{r suffstat-table}
sm_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(llm_sm), function(key) {
  p <- split_key(key)
  data.frame(Provider  = p$pname,
             Condition = condition_labels[match(p$cid, condition_ids)],
             as.data.frame(t(round(llm_sm[[key]], 3))),
             check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
emp_sm_row <- data.frame(Provider = "Empirical", Condition = "—",
                          as.data.frame(t(round(emp_sm, 3))),
                          check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(rbind(emp_sm_row, sm_tab), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Sufficient statistic means by provider and condition")
```

## 3. Key Findings

```{r rmse-table}
rmse_rows <- lapply(names(llm_sm), function(key) {
  p    <- split_key(key)
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((llm_sm[[key]] - emp_sm)^2))
  data.frame(Provider  = p$pname,
             Condition = condition_labels[match(p$cid, condition_ids)],
             RMSE      = round(rmse, 3),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
rmse_df <- do.call(rbind, rmse_rows)
rmse_df <- rmse_df[order(rmse_df$RMSE), ]
knitr::kable(rmse_df, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "RMSE of sufficient statistic means relative to empirical baseline (lower = better)")
```

**Sender roleplay outperforms other conditions for both providers.** Fixing the
sender identity and showing observed history forces the LLM to reason from a
specific actor's track record, which surfaces recency and repetition dynamics
more directly than unconstrained prediction or random roleplay.

**Recencylog is the largest gap across all conditions.** The empirical mean is
−5.46, reflecting sharp decay in the hazard for recently active dyads. LLM
sequences are substantially less negative, indicating that LLMs do not
adequately downweight dyads that were recently active — they spread events more
evenly across the risk set than the empirical data supports.

**NTriadic remains positive across all conditions.** The empirical mean is
effectively zero (0.001), masking a strong negative coefficient in the Cox
model. All LLM conditions produce positive NTriadic means, consistent with the
cross-provider sign reversal observed in prior work and reflecting an implicit
"enemy of my enemy" heuristic in the training data.

**Bedrock/Llama predict_obs is missing** from the sufficient statistic results
due to a computation failure on that sequence; it is present in the coefficient
comparison.
